claims.statement: The application's operating-system surface is partitioned by owner process: the outer guard owns explorer's desktop icon view and the HideIcons preference read, the --panel process owns the Startup folder link, the Electron shell APIs and its own window state, the data-plane utilityProcess owns the periodic process/registry/hardware/filesystem reads plus the userData writes, and the detached restore watcher only waits on the guard's process handle.

Every machine-level write in the application is non-fatal and either restorable or idempotent: a failed icon hide degrades to a logged two-desktops run, a failed autostart apply is caught inside bootPanel, a failed placement or usage-log write is swallowed, and neither a read nor a write is allowed to stop the panel from appearing.

Desktop icon visibility is changed by sending WM_COMMAND (0x0111) with parameter 0x7402 to the SHELLDLL_DefView window through SendMessageTimeoutW with SMTO_ABORTIFHUNG and a 3000 ms budget — the same command explorer's View menu issues — so a hung explorer degrades to a logged failure instead of wedging the guard.

The application writes no registry value on the icon path: explorer itself writes the resulting HideIcons REG_DWORD under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced as a side effect of the shell command, which is why every registry access in the application is a read.

Icon-state reasoning keeps two independent observations apart: iconsVisible() asks IsWindowVisible on the desktop SysListView32 and is the only authority for whether a toggle is needed, while prefHidden() reads the HideIcons preference and only decides whether this run may hide at all; the restore paths are view-fact-gated so icons a user re-showed during a run are never hidden again.

The Startup link is created and read through src/main/autostart.ps1, spawned as a standalone script with -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File, a 20 s timeout and UTF-8 stdout decoding; the caller parses the last non-empty stdout line as JSON and treats a non-zero exit as a real failure distinct from "the shortcut does not exist", while deletion is done in Node with fs.rmSync(force) and has no COM branch.

The PowerShell helper must stay ASCII-only because Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads a BOM-less script with the system ANSI code page (the same convention as accept/lib/capture.ps1 and uia-focus.ps1), it is invoked with -File rather than an inline -Command so argument values containing spaces are not re-parsed through cmd, and its argument parameter is $LinkArgs because $args is an automatic variable that would silently swallow the bound value.

Only a run whose app directory normalizes to the declared config.autostart.appDir may create the Startup link or adopt a dead one, a live link pointing elsewhere is never rewritten, enabled:false removes the link without requiring production identity, and the retired Python watchdog link is deleted unconditionally on every run.

Three writes cross into other applications, all best-effort and user-initiated: ShowWindow(SW_RESTORE) plus BringWindowToTop and SetForegroundWindow to raise a tool's window (a foreground-lock refusal degrades to action 'degraded'), shell.openPath (ShellExecute semantics) to start a tool or desktop item, and spawn('explorer', ['/select,', path]) to reveal a search result.

Every launch surface is fenced by who may name the path: a desktop item is started only if its path is in the current scanned pool, a search result only if it belongs to the latest result set, and a tool only from config.tools, so the renderer never supplies an executable path.

The panel writes its own window state directly: focusable:false (effectively WS_EX_NOACTIVATE), transparent, frameless, shadowless and skipTaskbar, mouse-transparent by default, with z-order forced to the bottom through SetWindowPos(HWND_BOTTOM, SWP_NOMOVE | SWP_NOSIZE | SWP_NOACTIVATE | SWP_NOOWNERZORDER) and re-pinned at startup, on hot-zone leave behind a 500 ms throttle, and on stray focus events.

Every FFI binding declares __stdcall with explicit argument and return types, passes out-parameters as Buffers and handles as void */uintptr_t, and is typed through a hand-written src/main/koffi.d.ts whose functions return any — so the signature string inside each func() call is the only contract.

Bindings are loaded in three shapes for a reason: eagerly at module load for modules reached only from an Electron entry point or a lazily-required source (win32.ts and icon-carry.ts through index.ts, net-counters.ts through require() in systemHardwareSources()), lazily and memoized in the first call for modules whose consumers are tested with injected fake sources (usage/native.ts, focus/adapter.ts, the attribute read in desktop/adapter.ts), and in its own process for the restore watcher.

Process enumeration reads only a pid to exe-path map: EnumProcesses fills a 4096-entry pid buffer, each pid is opened with OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION) and read with QueryFullProcessImageNameW into a 1024-byte buffer whose length field is pre-set to 510 wide characters, CloseHandle always runs in a finally, and windows or pids whose image path cannot be read are skipped rather than reported.

The foreground-window path never reads a window title: it resolves hwnd through GetWindowThreadProcessId to QueryFullProcessImageNameW, WindowCandidate has no title field at all, and a standing test walks every .ts file under src/main asserting that GetWindowText and window_title appear nowhere — a filter that excludes the .cjs watcher and the .ps1 helper from that scan.

The usage log records exactly {ts, exe} per line (asserted by test), which makes "frequency" mean real process starts with time decay and forces the document zone to sort by file modification time instead of reusing the same score.

Registry access is read-only and goes through the reg/reg.exe binaries: the HideIcons preference via spawnSync('reg', ['query', …]) matched by regex where no match reads as "not hidden", and the UserAssist launch counts via an async reg.exe export into a temp .reg file read back as UTF-16LE and parsed as text, taking only \Count subkeys and .exe/.lnk paths and resolving to an empty map on any failure.

Interface counters come from iphlpapi!GetIfTable walked with hand-validated flat MIB_IFROW offsets hardcoded in the module (860-byte rows, table body at offset 4, dwIndex at 512, dwInOctets at 552, dwOutOctets at 576) with one re-query on ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER, while the 32-bit counter wrap is handled in the pure rate layer rather than in the binding.

The GPU readout is an execFile of nvidia-smi with --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,memory.used,memory.total and --format=csv,noheader,nounits under a 5000 ms timeout and windowsHide, parsed from the first CSV line, cached and asynchronous so the 1 Hz sampling loop never blocks on the spawn; the production assembly sets a 5 s TTL even though the class default is 3 s, and a failure still occupies the TTL.

The desktop roots are the user desktop resolved through app.getPath('desktop') (which follows a OneDrive redirection) and the common desktop derived from the PUBLIC environment variable; both are watched with non-persistent fs.watch merged through a 300 ms settle timer, an unwatchable root is skipped silently, and the 1 Hz rescan is the documented backstop.

GetFileAttributesW is bound from kernel32 (explicitly not user32) and collapsed into one isHidden boolean from FILE_ATTRIBUTE_HIDDEN | FILE_ATTRIBUTE_SYSTEM; a lookup that fails with INVALID_FILE_ATTRIBUTES is treated as visible so an attribute failure never drops a desktop item.

Icon extraction and shortcut resolution are Electron-main-only capabilities (app.getFileIcon, shell.readShortcutLink), so the data-plane child runs with no icon face: .lnk targets are resolved through a batched proxy request back to the parent, which also pre-warms icons from every snapshot it receives.

app.getFileIcon returns a byte-identical generic icon for every .lnk on this machine, so the extractor resolves the icon source through shell.readShortcutLink first and a pure decision prefers the declared icon location, falls back to the target executable, and returns null when neither exists so the caller falls back to extracting from the .lnk itself.

Persistent state is written atomically or append-only: app/config.json and userData/layout.json use tmp plus rename (an unparsable config is never overwritten), usage day files are append-only with swallowed write failures and a 90-day prune, the evidence log only exists when DECK_EVENT_LOG is set, and plugin roots are created recursively before they are watched.

The Python-era usage log at %LOCALAPPDATA%\qoder-deck\usage is copied rather than moved into userData/usage, only for day files inside the retention window, with per-file bookkeeping for idempotency, and the legacy directory is deliberately left in place.

archive/wallpaper-assets/ holds the retired Wallpaper Engine-era asset trees frozen read-only since 2026-09-29, is referenced by no build, test or acceptance flow, and carries three standing rules: do not modify, do not depend on it, and deletion is allowed.

net-counters.ts's header still describes the module as loaded only in the main process, but the production assembly installs HardwareService inside the data-plane utilityProcess, so that comment is stale relative to the ADR-0005 split.

Test coverage stops short of two surfaces that matter for change planning: nothing exercises the PowerShell helper against a non-ASCII Startup path — the ASCII invariant constrains the script source while the caller decodes stdout as UTF-8 — and nothing exercises the hand-validated MIB_IFROW offsets on a different Windows build.

The acceptance harness deliberately re-binds its own user32/kernel32/imm32 copies instead of importing production code, so a probe cannot be silently fixed by the same edit that breaks the panel; its GetWindowTextW binding is the only window-title read in the application or harness.

Session collection reads other applications' stores without writing them: SQLite files are opened through node:sqlite with readOnly:true and PRAGMA busy_timeout=500 so a store locked by its writer fails fast instead of stalling the 1 Hz tick.

The UserAssist read is the one place the application ingests activity the operating system already recorded about the user, and it is deliberately implemented as an exported .reg text file parsed in pure code (the export escaping layer absorbs quotes and backslashes inside ROT13-obfuscated value names) with the export run asynchronously so it never sits on the boot critical path.
